title: Cap. X Arg. II close: adversaries confess an inscrutable good pleasure in preparing/not preparing efficacious grace — that pleasure precedes forescience of faith accepted or grace finally rejected; they may not affirm the reverse
pass_a_gloss: You see what the adversaries themselves confess: from which let us conclude that there is in preparing and not preparing efficacious grace a certain secret and inscrutable good pleasure of God, which does not follow the forescience of faith and of accepted grace in the elect, and the forescience of unbelief and of grace finally rejected in the reprobate, but precedes the forescience of both. For he would be ridiculous who should say that from the decree of providence grace only sufficient is prepared for some, with certain forescience that it will be rejected, and that unto the same from the decree of reprobation efficacious grace is denied, which is refused by no hard heart, and afterward should teach that this is done because God foresaw that these would reject his grace and die in their unbelief and pertinacity. They therefore who dare not deny the former ought not so confidently to have affirmed the latter.
pass_b_english: You see what the adversaries themselves confess. From that let us conclude: in preparing and not preparing efficacious grace there is a secret, inscrutable good pleasure of God. It does not follow forescience of faith and accepted grace in the elect, or forescience of unbelief and grace finally rejected in the reprobate — it precedes both. For it would be ridiculous to say that from the providence decree only sufficient grace is prepared for some, with certain forescience it will be rejected, and that from the reprobation decree efficacious grace — which no hard heart refuses — is denied them, and then to teach that this happens because God foresaw they would reject his grace and die in unbelief and pertinacity. Those who dare not deny the first ought not so confidently to have affirmed the second.
source_text: Videtis quid ipsi adversarii fateantur: ex quibus concludamus, esse in praeparanda et non praeparanda gratia efficaci arcanum quoddam et inscrutabile beneplacitum Dei, quod non sequitur praescientiam fidei et gratiae acceptatae in electis, ac praescientiam infidelitatis et gratiae finaliter rejectae in reprobatis, sed utriusque praescientiam antecedit. Ridiculus enim fuerit qui diceret, ex decreto providentiae praeparari aliquibus gratiam solummodo sufficientem, cum praescientia certa quod rejicietur, atque iisdem ex decreto reprobationis negari gratiam efficacem, quae a nullo duro corde respuitur, ac postea doceret hoc fieri quia Deus praevidebat hosce gratiam suam rejecturos et in sua infidelitate et pertinacia morituros. Qui igitur prius non audent negare, non debuerunt posterius tam confidenter affirmare.
